title: E2a — Config model types and Tomlyn binding
description:
Immutable model types for config/hosts.toml, bound with Tomlyn.

Shape is docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md exactly: a [global] block, and per-host [hosts.<key>] with nested .mount, .session and .probe tables.

- Records/immutable types; the config is read-only once loaded
- The host's TOML KEY (e.g. `example-nas`) is the stable identity throughout the system. display_name is presentation only. Keep them distinct in the model - a downstream decision (bs-08g) turns on this.
- Global defaults applied when a key is absent, including mounted_probe_interval_seconds = 60 (ADR-011)
- Parse failures surface the TOML line/column; a config error the user cannot locate is a bad error

Do NOT implement validation rules here - that is bs-? (E2b). This issue is parse and bind only.

Acceptance: config/hosts.example.toml parses into the model with every field populated as written, asserted field by field. Malformed TOML produces a diagnostic naming the position.

title: E2c — IHostConfigStore: load, watch, reload, retain-last-valid
description:
The store that owns the live config and its reload lifecycle.

- Load and validate at startup
- Watch config/hosts.toml and re-load on write
- Emit a change event consumers subscribe to
- INVALID CONFIG IS REJECTED WHOLESALE. Never partially applied. The store keeps serving the LAST VALID config and surfaces the error (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6: "Keep running on the last valid config; surface the parse error").
- Debounce/coalesce file writes: editors write in bursts and often truncate-then-write, so a naive watcher fires on a zero-byte intermediate state. Retry a failed read briefly before declaring the config invalid - a transient read failure mid-save is NOT a validation error and must not evict the last valid config.

That debounce point is the subtle part of this issue and the most likely source of a real bug.

Threading: consumers read an immutable snapshot. The store never hands out mutable state.

Acceptance: deterministic tests with an injected filesystem/clock - no Thread.Sleep, no reliance on real FileSystemWatcher timing in unit tests. Cover: valid load; write a valid change and observe the event; write an invalid change and assert the PREVIOUS config is still served and an error surfaced; simulate a truncated mid-write read and assert the last valid config survives.

title: E2b — Config validation rules
description:
Every validation rule in docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md, each producing a distinct, locatable error.

Rules (reject the WHOLE config if any fail):
- duplicate host key or duplicate display_name
- two hosts claiming the same drive letter
- mode != "none" with no drive or no remote_path
- drive not matching ^[D-Z]:$ (A-C reserved)
- vfs_cache_mode in {off, minimal}
- identity_file path does not resolve to an existing file
- backoff_seconds empty or containing non-positive values
- probe.interval_seconds negative
- global.mounted_probe_interval_seconds zero or negative (ABSENT IS NOT AN ERROR - defaults to 60, ADR-011)

Why each matters, so you can judge edge cases: duplicate display_name is not cosmetic - E7 emits Terminal profiles named from it, and `wt -p "<name>"` has undocumented tie-breaking on collisions, so uniqueness here is what makes profile launching deterministic. vfs_cache_mode below writes breaks editors and Office outright (Invariant I6). Drive collisions must never be auto-resolved (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6).

Validation must be a pure function over the parsed model - no I/O except the identity_file existence check, which must be injectable so tests do not depend on the developer's ~/.ssh contents.

Acceptance: one test per rule, each failing for exactly one describable reason. A config violating two rules reports both, not just the first. A valid config produces no errors.
notes:
ADR-011 acceptance criteria absorbed from bs-ugm (superseded):
- A config OMITTING mounted_probe_interval_seconds parses and yields 60. Absent is NOT an error.
- mounted_probe_interval_seconds = 0 is rejected; the previous config is retained.
- mounted_probe_interval_seconds negative is rejected.
- probe.interval_seconds negative is rejected.
- probe.interval_seconds = 0 PARSES - it is the documented on-demand default (ADR-008) and must not be rejected.
The binding and the default-60 behaviour belong to bs-0na (E2a); the two rejection rules belong here.

title: E1b — Generic Host and WPF App bootstrap
description:
Wire the WPF application to Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.

- App.xaml with NO StartupUri and ShutdownMode=OnExplicitShutdown (the app has no main window; it will be tray-driven in E9)
- App.xaml.cs builds an IHost, starts it on OnStartup, stops it with a bounded timeout on OnExit
- DI container available for the services listed in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2, registered as they arrive in later epics
- Unhandled-exception logging for both AppDomain and Dispatcher

Spec: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2 (process model) — one process, no main window, BackgroundService supervisor. Invariant I3: the supervisor is in-process in the user's interactive session, never a Windows Service.

Acceptance: host starts and stops cleanly under test without a window; unit test asserts the host builds and resolves its registrations. Do NOT run the application.

title: E1a — Solution skeleton, projects, and build properties
description:
Create the repository's build skeleton.

- Bosun.sln at repo root
- src/Bosun/Bosun.csproj — TFM net10.0-windows, UseWPF=true, OutputType WinExe
- tests/Bosun.Tests/Bosun.Tests.csproj — xUnit, references src/Bosun
- Directory.Build.props — Nullable=enable, TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, LangVersion latest (C# 14), ImplicitUsings as appropriate
- .editorconfig with C# formatting/analyzer rules

Hard constraints:
- NEVER set PublishTrimmed anywhere. Trimming is unsupported for WPF and fails at runtime in non-obvious ways.
- Use `dotnet new` / `dotnet add package` / `dotnet sln add`. Do not hand-edit package references into .csproj.

Acceptance: `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` both succeed and are warning-clean from the repo root.

title: E2 — Configuration layer: TOML schema, load, validate, watch
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E2. Spec: docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md.

- TOML schema per docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md, bound with Tomlyn
- IHostConfigStore: load, validate, watch-and-reload
- Validation: duplicate host names, drive-letter collisions, malformed drive letters, missing identity files, mode = "persistent" without a drive letter
- Invalid config must be rejected wholesale — never partially applied. Keep running on the last valid config and surface the error.
- Unit tests: valid parse, each validation failure, reload on change

Send test-author alongside implementer here (CLAUDE.md §6): config validation is one of the three areas where a misread spec becomes a hung Explorer rather than a red test.

title: E1 — Foundation: solution layout, host bootstrap, logging
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E1. No dependencies; start here.

- Solution and project layout: src/Bosun/, tests/Bosun.Tests/, Bosun.sln
- Target net10.0-windows, UseWPF=true, nullable enabled, warnings as errors
- Generic Host bootstrap; WPF App with ShutdownMode=OnExplicitShutdown and no StartupUri
- Serilog to a rolling file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bosun\logs\ plus debug sink
- .editorconfig, Directory.Build.props
- Verify dotnet build and dotnet test pass in CI

Constraints: never set PublishTrimmed (unsupported for WPF, fails at runtime in non-obvious ways). Build must stay warning-clean.

Decompose into tasks before starting.

title: E5 — Mount supervisor: the state machine
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E5. THE CORE OF THE PROJECT — build and test this before any UI.

- State machine exactly as specified in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4
- Single-threaded async loop; per-host transitions serialised through one channel
- Reconciliation against mount/listmounts every tick
- Adopt-or-clear existing mounts on startup (crash recovery)
- Idle-unmount timer for on-demand hosts
- Forced-unmount escalation when a clean unmount does not confirm
- Extensive unit tests on the transition table: every transition, every guard, every timeout path

Invariants: I1 (Mounting reachable only from Ready, only after a passing deep probe), I2 (N consecutive failures → unmount immediately; never retry through failure). Only IMountSupervisor calls mount/mount and mount/unmount.

Send test-author independently (CLAUDE.md §6). Critical path and highest risk — do not let UI work start before the transition table is under test.

title: Probe mounted hosts even when interval_seconds = 0 (ADR-011)
description:
Implement the ADR-011 probe-scheduling split in the supervisor.

Rule (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4 rule 3):
- probe.interval_seconds governs polling while a host is IDLE (Ready, Unreachable) only. 0 = do not poll while idle.
- A host in Mounted is ALWAYS probed. Effective interval:
    interval_seconds > 0  → min(interval_seconds, global.mounted_probe_interval_seconds)
    interval_seconds == 0 → global.mounted_probe_interval_seconds

Why this exists: without it, an on-demand host with interval_seconds = 0 (the documented default, and what config/hosts.example.toml ships for example-remote) is never probed once mounted, so it never accumulates failures, never reaches Draining, and leaves a drive letter pointing at a dead host. That is an Invariant I2 violation and the exact wedged-Explorer failure the project exists to prevent.

Acceptance criteria:
- A mounted host with interval_seconds = 0 is probed at mounted_probe_interval_seconds and reaches Draining after failures_before_unmount consecutive failures.
- A host with interval_seconds = 3600 is probed at mounted_probe_interval_seconds while mounted (clamped), not at 3600.
- A host with interval_seconds = 15 is probed at 15 while mounted (not clamped up).
- An on-demand host in Ready with interval_seconds = 0 generates NO probe traffic — the ADR-008 behaviour must not regress.
- Tests are deterministic with injected time; no sleeps, no real clock, fake IProbe.

title: needs-decision: profile identity vs host renames (E7)
description:
Surfaced by verified research into Terminal's fragment GUID derivation (see bs-3ir design notes).

Terminal derives a fragment profile's GUID as UUIDv5(UUIDv5(TERMINAL_FRAGMENT_NS, app-name), profile-name). The GUID is therefore a hash of the profile NAME.

Consequence: if a host's profile name changes in config/hosts.toml, the derived GUID changes, and Terminal treats it as an entirely new profile. Any customisation the user layered onto the old profile in their own settings.json (keyed by the old GUID) is silently orphaned, and the renamed host appears fresh and uncustomised.

This mechanism is directly documented. The user-facing consequence is inferred from it (high confidence mechanically, but not spelled out by Microsoft as a warning).

Options:
  A. Treat host profile names as immutable identity once created. Simplest; costs the user the ability to rename a host without losing Terminal-side customisation. Document it.
  B. Emit an explicit stable `guid` derived by Bosun from the host's config KEY (e.g. `hosts.example-nas`) rather than its display_name. Renames of display_name then preserve identity. Costs us owning the GUID derivation and a migration story for anyone who already has profiles.
  C. Do nothing and accept silent orphaning on rename.

Recommendation: B. The config key is already the stable identifier everywhere else in the system, display_name is explicitly a presentation field, and B costs one UUIDv5 implementation we can verify against Microsoft's own published test vector (app "Git", profile "Git Bash" -> {2ece5bfe-50ed-5f3a-ab87-5cd4baafed2b}).

BLOCKS E7 implementation. Do not guess - this is an identity contract that is painful to change after users have profiles.

title: E1c — Serilog rolling-file logging
description:
Serilog wired into the Generic Host.

- Rolling daily file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bosun\logs\ plus a debug sink
- Structured output; the log path must be injectable so tests never write to the real %LOCALAPPDATA% location
- Integrated via Microsoft.Extensions.Logging so ILogger<T> injection works throughout

Why it matters: docs/OPERATIONS.md makes the log the primary triage artifact — every state transition will be logged with host, from-state, to-state, and trigger (E5). Get the shape right now so E5 can just use it.

Acceptance: a test writes to a temp log path and asserts the file is produced and parseable; no test writes to the real %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bosun\logs\.

title: E7 — Windows Terminal fragment writer
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E7. Spec: ADR-006.

- Verify the current fragment directory for Store vs unpackaged Terminal against Microsoft documentation before implementing — do not hardcode from memory
- Serialise host list to fragment schema: name, commandline, colour scheme, tab colour, icon
- tmux variant: ssh -t <host> tmux new -A -s <session>
- Optional reconnect wrapper script generation (retry on exit 255, exit cleanly on 0)
- Rewrite on config change; never touch settings.json
- Test: fragment is valid JSON, Terminal loads it, wt -w 0 new-tab -p "<host>" opens a session

Invariant I5. Tests write to a temp directory injected via the interface, never the real Fragments\Bosun\ path.

Good first task for the researcher subagent: the fragment directory and schema are an area where secondhand information is routinely wrong.
design:
VERIFIED against Microsoft Learn (ms.date 2025-11-10, fetched 2026-08-16), per ADR-006's instruction to verify rather than hardcode.

FRAGMENT PATH (high confidence)
Two supported locations, both read regardless of whether Terminal itself is Store or unpackaged:
  all-users:  C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\{app}\{file}.json
  per-user:   %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\{app}\{file}.json
Bosun is an unpackaged per-user win-x64 EXE, so use the per-user path:
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\Bosun\bosun.json
NOTE the "Microsoft\" path segment - ADR-006 and CLAUDE.md I5 both abbreviate this as
"...\Windows Terminal\Fragments\Bosun\" and omit it. The Store-vs-unpackaged distinction in
ADR-006's note is a red herring: it applies only to Store-PACKAGED APPS registering via an
app-extension manifest (PublicFolder\Fragments), which is a different mechanism Bosun does not use.
Terminal Preview: docs do not state a separate Fragments dir; this sub-point is inferred, not sourced.

SCHEMA (high confidence)
Top level: two optional arrays, "profiles" and "schemes".
Profile entries are either new profiles (name REQUIRED) or {"updates": "{guid}", ...overrides}.
Fragments accept the full standard profile object - name, commandline, startingDirectory, icon,
colorScheme, tabColor all supported.
icon: relative paths resolve against the fragment dir only on Terminal >= 1.24; web URLs otherwise.
startingDirectory: the docs self-contradict on the default (states %USERPROFILE%, then lists four
launch-context-dependent defaults). SET IT EXPLICITLY per host rather than relying on any default.
Fragment "schemes" entries must define name plus ALL 16 colour-table entries; partial schemes rejected.

PROFILE GUID (high confidence - refines ADR-006's wording)
UUIDv5, two-level derivation:
  appNamespace = UUIDv5(TERMINAL_FRAGMENT_NS, app-name), TERMINAL_FRAGMENT_NS = {f65ddb7e-706b-4499-8a50-40313caf510a}
  profileGuid  = UUIDv5(appNamespace, profile-name)
Name strings encoded UTF-16LE before hashing.
Documented test vector: app "Git", profile "Git Bash" -> {2ece5bfe-50ed-5f3a-ab87-5cd4baafed2b}.
USE THAT AS A UNIT TEST. If our derivation reproduces it, the implementation is right.
Emitting "guid" ourselves is optional but "strongly encouraged" by the docs. Recommended: omit it and
let Terminal derive, treating (app-name, profile-name) as the identity contract - but see bs- issue on
renames before committing to that.

COLOUR SCHEME SCOPE (medium-high confidence)
Scheme names live in one global namespace merged from the user's settings.json and all fragments.
A fragment profile may reference a scheme the user defined. Collision behaviour for duplicate scheme
names is NOT documented anywhere on Learn - a real documentation gap.

FAILURE MODES (medium confidence - sourced from the Terminal repo, not Learn; Learn is silent)
Since microsoft/terminal#10601 (fixes #10590, shipped 1.10.1933.0), Terminal wraps per-fragment parsing
in try/catch: a malformed fragment is skipped and other fragments still load. Before that, one bad
fragment broke all of them.
There is NO UI surface, toast, or default log indicating a fragment failed to load. So: validate our
own JSON before writing it, and treat "profiles appear in Terminal's dropdown" as the only available
confirmation. docs/OPERATIONS.md "Terminal profiles missing" triage should say this.
microsoft/terminal#13916: removing a profile reference from a fragment does not always take effect
cleanly - relevant when a host is deleted from hosts.toml.

wt.exe (high confidence)
`wt -w 0 new-tab -p "<profile name>"` is current. -w 0 is documented as "most recently used window".
-p takes the profile NAME; quote names containing spaces.
Duplicate/ambiguous profile names: undocumented tie-breaking, and an unrecognised name appears to fall
back silently rather than error (microsoft/terminal#6086). ALREADY MITIGATED: docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md
validation already rejects duplicate display_name, so E2 enforces the uniqueness E7 depends on.
Cross-check that rule survives E2 implementation.

title: E3 — rclone rc client and rcd process lifecycle
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E3. Spec: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3.

- RcloneProcessService: start rclone rcd on a configurable loopback port, health-check via core/version, restart on death, stop cleanly on exit
- IRcloneClient typed wrapper: config/create, config/get, mount/mount, mount/unmount, mount/listmounts, operations/list
- Ensure an sftp remote exists per configured host, derived from config
- WinFsp presence detection at startup with an actionable message
- Integration tests against a real rclone rcd where feasible; otherwise a fake

Invariant I4: all mount operations go through the rc HTTP API, never by spawning rclone mount. Only IMountSupervisor may call mount/mount and mount/unmount — IRcloneClient exposes them, nothing else invokes them.

Anything touching a real rclone rcd or WinFsp is a MARKED INTEGRATION TEST excluded from the default suite.

title: E8 — Session monitor: ssh.exe enumeration and TCP state
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E8. Spec: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3 (ISessionMonitor).

- Enumerate ssh.exe via Process.GetProcessesByName
- Resolve command lines via CIM to correlate process → configured host
- GetExtendedTcpTable P/Invoke for socket state
- All of it behind ISessionMonitor, faked in tests
- Isolated in one file; this is the ugliest code in the project

P/Invoke must not leak beyond the ISessionMonitor implementation — the validator checks this explicitly. If interop starts appearing in a second file, stop and escalate.

title: E4 — Probe engine: shallow, deep, backoff ladder
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E4. Spec: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3 (IProbe) and §4.

- Shallow probe: TCP connect with timeout
- Deep probe: operations/list root, depth 1 — proves auth and SFTP subsystem
- Backoff ladder with reset triggers (network change, resume, manual retry)
- IProbe fakeable for tests

TCP success does not imply SFTP success — never mount on a shallow probe alone (Invariant I1). Probe scheduling is state-dependent, not purely config-driven: see ADR-011 and bs child issue on mounted-host probing.

title: E6 — System event integration: power, network, session
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E6. Spec: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3 (ISystemEventSource).

- PowerModeChanged Suspend → unmount all, bounded time budget (suspend_unmount_timeout_seconds, default 8s — Windows will not wait forever)
- PowerModeChanged Resume → re-probe all, bypass backoff
- NetworkAddressChanged → reset backoff, force-probe mounted hosts
- Test with real sleep/resume and a real network change; manual protocol in docs/OPERATIONS.md T1/T2

Invariant I8. docs/OPERATIONS.md T2 (close lid on LAN, open on another network, nothing wedged) is the acceptance test that matters for v1.

Send test-author independently (CLAUDE.md §6).

title: Validate mounted_probe_interval_seconds and probe intervals (ADR-011)
description:
Config-layer half of ADR-011.

- Bind new global setting mounted_probe_interval_seconds. Default 60 when absent.
- Reject the whole config if probe.interval_seconds is negative.
- Reject the whole config if mounted_probe_interval_seconds is zero or negative. ABSENT IS NOT AN ERROR - it defaults to 60, consistent with every other [global] field. Rejecting a config for a newly-introduced key would break every existing hosts.toml on upgrade.
- Rejection semantics are unchanged: whole config refused, previous config retained, error surfaced.

Spec: docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md (global block, field semantics table, validation rules) and ADR-011.

Acceptance criteria:
- A config omitting mounted_probe_interval_seconds parses and yields 60.
- mounted_probe_interval_seconds = 0 is rejected; the previous config is retained.
- mounted_probe_interval_seconds negative is rejected.
- probe.interval_seconds negative is rejected.
- probe.interval_seconds = 0 parses (it is the documented on-demand default).
- One test per rule, each failing for one describable reason.

title: Install WinFsp and rclone on the dev machine
description:
Neither WinFsp nor rclone is currently installed on the maintainer's machine (verified: `rclone` not on PATH, C:\Program Files (x86)\WinFsp absent). dotnet 10.0.302, Windows Terminal, uv, bd and graphify are all present.

This does not block E1, E2, E4, E7, or E8 — those are fully fakeable. It blocks E3 integration tests, any real mount, and every manual protocol in docs/OPERATIONS.md.

Run scripts/dev-setup.ps1 (idempotent; installs both via winget).

Human task — an agent should not install system software on the maintainer's daily driver.

title: Startup failures before the host is built are logged nowhere
description:
Found while validating E1 (src/Bosun/App.xaml.cs).

App.OnStartup registers the AppDomain and Dispatcher unhandled-exception handlers, then calls BosunHostFactory.CreateHost(), then resolves ILogger<App> into _logger. Both handlers log via `_logger?.` — a null-conditional.

So any exception thrown BEFORE the logger is resolved is swallowed entirely: no file, no debug sink, no window. CreateHost() can genuinely throw here — it calls Directory.CreateDirectory on %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bosun\logs, which fails on a permissions problem, a redirected/roaming profile, or a full disk. The user would see Bosun fail to start with no diagnostic anywhere, which is the worst possible failure shape for a tray app with no window.

This is not hypothetical for the target environment: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-010 explicitly courts users on corporate VPNs and domain-joined machines, where redirected AppData is common.

Fix direction: get a minimal bootstrap logger (Serilog self-log, or a file write to a path that cannot fail, or the Windows Event Log) installed BEFORE CreateHost() is called, so the pre-host window is covered. Whatever is chosen must not itself throw.

Acceptance: a test forces CreateHost() to throw (e.g. an unwritable log directory) and asserts a diagnostic is produced somewhere durable.

title: needs-decision: should Bosun survive a DispatcherUnhandledException? (E9)
description:
Raised by the E1 implementer and deliberately not guessed at.

src/Bosun/App.xaml.cs OnDispatcherUnhandledException currently LOGS ONLY and does not set e.Handled = true, so a dispatcher exception still terminates the process. That is the right conservative default for E1, where there is no UI at all.

Once the tray icon exists (E9) the tradeoff changes and needs a real decision:
  A. Keep terminating. Honest, but a transient UI glitch in the status window kills the supervisor, which silently stops probing and unmounting. For a tool whose entire purpose is reacting to hosts going away, dying quietly is arguably the worst outcome.
  B. Set e.Handled = true, log, and show a balloon. The supervisor keeps running. Risk: the app limps along in an unknown state, which is how a mount gets left up while its host is gone — an Invariant I2 violation by a different route.
  C. Split the difference: handle exceptions originating from UI code, terminate on anything from the supervisor path.

The I2 angle is what makes this more than a style question, and it is why it should be decided deliberately rather than defaulted. Note that terminating the process is NOT automatically safe either: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 already requires adopt-or-clear of existing mounts on the next start, so a crash with mounts up is a handled case — but only if the user restarts Bosun.

Decide during E9, alongside the balloon-notification work.

title: needs-decision: should the fragment ship custom colour schemes? (E7)
description:
Surfaced by verified research (see bs-3ir design notes).

A fragment may declare colour schemes in a top-level "schemes" array, and scheme names resolve in ONE GLOBAL NAMESPACE merged from the user's settings.json and every installed fragment. Microsoft documents no collision or precedence behaviour for duplicate scheme names - a genuine documentation gap, not something we can look up.

docs/CONFIG-SCHEMA.md gives each host a `session.color_scheme` (example config uses "Campbell", a Terminal built-in) and a separate `session.tab_color`. So today Bosun only REFERENCES scheme names; it does not define any.

Options:
  A. Reference existing scheme names only; never emit a "schemes" array. Zero collision risk. The user must have the named scheme already, and validation cannot check that (we cannot read settings.json - Invariant I5).
  B. Ship one namespaced Bosun scheme (e.g. "Bosun Default") as a fallback. Small collision risk, better first-run experience.

Recommendation: A, for v1. It matches ADR-010's warning against premature generalisation, and the example config already uses a Terminal built-in. Revisit only if a real host needs a scheme that does not exist.

Note the interaction with I5: because we must never read settings.json, an invalid colour_scheme name cannot be validated and will fail silently at Terminal's end. Worth surfacing in docs/OPERATIONS.md triage regardless of which option is chosen.

title: Amend ADR-006 and I5 with the verified fragment path and GUID algorithm
description:
ADR-006's implementation note asked for exactly this verification; it is now done (bs-3ir design notes) and two details in the spec need correcting.

1. PATH. ADR-006 and CLAUDE.md Invariant I5 both write the fragment location as "...\Windows Terminal\Fragments\Bosun\", omitting the "Microsoft\" segment. The verified per-user path is:
     %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\Bosun\bosun.json

2. THE STORE-VS-UNPACKAGED NOTE IS A RED HERRING. ADR-006 says "The fragment directory differs between Store and unpackaged Terminal installs." Verified: it does not. Both the ProgramData and LocalAppData Fragments directories are read regardless of how Terminal itself was installed. The Store distinction applies only to Store-PACKAGED APPLICATIONS registering profiles via an app-extension manifest (PublicFolder\Fragments), a different mechanism that an unpackaged win-x64 EXE like Bosun does not use. Replace the note with the verified fact so nobody re-litigates it.

3. GUID WORDING. ADR-006 says fragments "yield stable profile GUIDs derived from source name plus profile name". Directionally right; the precise mechanism is UUIDv5 over a fixed namespace, two levels deep. Record the algorithm and the published test vector.

CLAUDE.md I5's substance (never read, write, or merge settings.json) is CORRECT and must not change - only the path text.

Caution: CLAUDE.md §2 is mirrored into the five .claude/agents/*.md definitions, which carry their own copies of the load-bearing rules. If I5's text changes, check whether the agent definitions quote the path and keep them in sync (CLAUDE.md §6 says both are reviewed artifacts).

Do this alongside E7 implementation, not before - the path should be proven by working code first.

title: CLAUDE.md §3 references `bd sync`, which does not exist in bd 1.2.2
description:
CLAUDE.md §3 says: "When you finish a unit of work, close its issue and run `bd sync` so the JSONL lands in git alongside the code." There is no `bd sync` command in the installed bd 1.1.0 — the command list has no such entry.

What actually happens now: bd 1.1.0 uses Dolt, storing issue data in .beads/embeddeddolt/, which .beads/.gitignore excludes. So issue state does NOT reach git by default and would not survive a fresh clone.

Mitigation already applied during seeding: `bd config set export.auto true` and `export.path issues.jsonl`, so .beads/issues.jsonl is written after write commands (throttled ~60s) and can be committed. This preserves the documented intent ("the JSONL export is committed, the SQLite db is not" — root .gitignore).

Decision needed from the maintainer:
1. Update CLAUDE.md §3 to say `bd export` + commit (or just 'commit .beads/issues.jsonl'), replacing the `bd sync` reference; and
2. Decide whether to also use Dolt remotes (`bd dolt push` to origin, already wired by bd init as git+https://github.com/bbuehne/bosun.git) or keep JSONL-only. Note bd init configured that remote but nothing has been pushed to it.

Also stale: root .gitignore's Beads block still mentions the SQLite db (.beads/*.db), which is the pre-Dolt layout.
notes:
UPDATE after upgrading bd 1.1.0 -> 1.2.2 (2026-08-16):

`bd sync` still does not exist, and now we know why. Per `bd info --whats-new`,
v1.2.2 is a RE-RELEASE of the tested 1.1 line (identical code to v1.1.2), issued
to supersede the accidental, untested v1.2.0/v1.2.1. The release note states
explicitly that the 1.2.x-only features -- leases, events journal, **bd sync**,
serve HTTP API, provenance -- are NOT included.

So `bd sync` existed only in a pulled, untested release. It is not a syntax drift
we can wait out, and it may never return under that name. CLAUDE.md §3 should be
corrected rather than left pending.

Also confirmed from the changelog (v1.0.5): "JSONL auto-export and auto-staging
are now opt-in - set export.auto=true and export.git-add=true to keep the old
behavior. Dolt is the canonical store." This validates enabling export.auto
during seeding. Consider also setting export.git-add=true so .beads/issues.jsonl
is staged automatically rather than remembered by hand.

Upgrade itself was clean: 15 issues, 13 edges, no cycles, no schema migration
required (our DB was created by 1.1.0 and never touched by the withdrawn v1.2.1,
which is the case that would have refused to open).
RESOLVED in CLAUDE.md §3 on 2026-08-16: the `bd sync` reference is replaced with "commit .beads/issues.jsonl", plus a note that export.auto is enabled, that `bd export` forces a refresh, and that the Dolt DB is gitignored so the commit is what makes the graph survive a clone.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md §3 corrected; bd sync confirmed absent in 1.2.2 (withdrawn 1.2.x-only feature)

title: E10 — Packaging, autostart, and release
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E10.

- dotnet publish single-file self-contained win-x64
- PublishTrimmed must remain off — trimming is unsupported for WPF
- Autostart via shell:startup shortcut, toggleable in the UI
- release.yml builds on tag and attaches the exe to a GitHub Release
- First-run experience: detect missing WinFsp / rclone / config, guide to setup

.github/workflows/release.yml already exists and already omits PublishTrimmed deliberately.

title: E9 — Tray UI: icon, context menu, status window
description:
Seeded from docs/WORK-BREAKDOWN.md E9.

- H.NotifyIcon tray with aggregate status in the icon
- Context menu: per-host mount/unmount, open terminal, open in Explorer
- Status window: table of hosts — state, drive, session count, last probe
- Actions post commands to the supervisor channel; UI never mutates state
- Colour coding matching per-host config
- Balloon notification on unexpected unmount — this is the user-visible consequence of ADR-005 and must not be silent

Do not start before E5's transition table is under test.
